html:
On 25 September 1513 the Spanish conquistador Vasco Núñez de Balboa saw the Pacific Ocean from a ridge in Darién, the first European to see it from the Americas.

He had heard from Indigenous people of a great sea to the south, and crossed the isthmus of Panama from the settlement of Santa María la Antigua del Darién with Spanish soldiers and Indigenous guides. A few days later he waded into the water and claimed the sea, which he called the South Sea, and all its shores for the crown of Castile.

The crossing showed that the lands Columbus had reached were not Asia, and that another ocean lay beyond them. It opened the way to Pizarro's conquest of Peru, launched from the Pacific side of the isthmus.
sum: On 25 September 1513 the Spanish conquistador Vasco Núñez de Balboa saw the Pacific Ocean from a ridge in Darién, the first European to see it from the Americas.
